sites.rationale: [Literature audit 2026-11-05 (deliverome-analysis PR 236): site added. The paper (PMID 26794006) was cited by KCNK5-internal-214-lit, which filed it under the wrong gene; the audit recovered the real site on KCNK3 at L214|Q (numbering: full-length human TASK-1 (KCNK3, NM_002246) numbering, inferred: UniProt P2-M4 extracellular loop is 205-222 and 214 lies inside it; if Δi20 removed 20 residues upstream, position 214 of the deleted protein would be 234 (inside M4), contradicting the stated loop; the construct was built on the Δi20 variant, whose deletion is not defined in the accessible text (ref 13, Rinné 2015 JMCC, PMID 25655935, is paywalled); construct species: human; paper reports surface: yes, function: not_reported). Paper: "was inserted in the extracellular P2-M4 loop of human TASK-Δi20 at amino acid position 214". Audit note: Original row named KCNK5/TASK-2 (wrong gene). Surface = chemiluminescence ELISA on intact (non-permeabilized) Xenopus oocytes with rat anti-HA (Fig 2c, WT-HA, and all alanine mutants on the WT-HA background); anti-HA westerns on oocyte lysates (Fig 3). TEVC currents (Fig 2b) are reported for wild-type and mutant TASK-1 without stating that the HA construct was recorded, so function of the tagged channel is not explicitly shown. All mutant alanine positions (L48-L62 etc.) are quoted in full-length numbering consistent with UniProt (L48, Y52, N53, L54, S55, Y59, L62 all match O14649), supporting full-length numbering for 214 as well.]

sites.rationale: L1 names the junction explicitly as between position 50 (Ala) and position 51 (Arg); Python lookup confirms seq[49]='A' and seq[50]='R', both matching the paper's residue identities exactly. The site sits 21 residues from the TM1 C-boundary (residue 29) and 58 residues from the TM2 N-boundary (residue 108), satisfying the ≥3-residue clearance rule on both sides. It is 46 residues upstream of the GYG selectivity-filter motif (residues 95–97), placing it well away from the pore-forming region. L2 independently confirms that the HA tag is accessible on the extracellular surface of intact cells. Full-length human TASK-1 (KCNK3) construct with an HA epitope tag inserted between A50 and R51 in the first extracellular loop (ECL1, residues 30–107), expressed in mammalian cells. L2 confirms surface display: intact cells were blocked, fixed, and incubated with anti-HA antibody, detecting the tag on the extracellular face.

sources.claim: An HA epitope was added to the extracellular loop of TASK-1 between positions 50 (Ala) and 51 (Arg) for the extracellularly tagged TASK-1.
